3.18.m:
the great-souled sky-dwellers of prowess equal to Śakra, / the gandharvas and apsarases, and whatever auspicious hosts of spirits [there be],
arrive in bodily form to the cherished great festival of the god. / Beholding the festival there, a man will surely become a sharer in good fortune.
There no injury must ever be done to the deity's property; / whether a king or one appointed by him, whoever is placed in authority there [and does injury],
he goes to a dreadful hell along with his sons, cattle, and relatives; / in this world, the destruction of his position will surely come to pass.
Those men who are devoted there, along with their livestock and store of wealth, / continually attain increase through the grace of the God of gods.
This dwelling of the lord of heaven built by another is to be seen, O moon among kings; / for having seen [it], a human being is freed from all sins and will obtain merit.

द्वारं च मध्यमं तस्य समदिक्स्थं प्रशस्यते ॥
द्वारं विस्तरतः कार्यं भूपाल द्विगुणोच्छ्रयम्॥2॥
गृहस्थस्य तु द्वारेण द्वारदेवकुलद्रुमैः ॥
अविद्धं तच्च कर्तव्यं नाम्बुस्रावि न कुक्षिमत्॥3॥
वज्रमध्यं नतं चैव द्वारं यत्नाद्विवर्जयेत॥
मङ्गल्यं रूपकोपेतं तच्च कार्यं प्रयत्नतः॥4॥
द्वारमानाष्टभागानां प्रतिमां तु सपिण्डिकाम्॥
द्वौ भागौ प्रतिमा तत्र तृतीयांशश्च पिण्डिका॥9॥
कटिरष्टमभागोनं द्वारं कार्यं विजानता॥
तृतीयमंशं वसुधा तृतीयांशः कटिर्भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
मंजरी च तृतीयांशः प्रासादस्य महाभुज ॥
गर्भं पादेन विस्तीर्ण तथा द्वारं प्रशस्यते ॥ 7 ॥
भित्तिर्गर्भाष्टभागोना तथा कार्या विजानता ॥
प्रासादोच्छ्रायभागेन चतुर्थेन च शस्यते ॥ 8 ॥
3.18.m:
And its central door facing directly toward a cardinal point is praised; / the door should be made with a height twice its width, O king.
It should be constructed unpierced by the door of a householder, / by gates, shrines, or trees; it should not discharge water, nor have a bulging belly.
One should diligently avoid a door that is narrow in the middle or bent; / and it should be made with careful effort auspicious and endowed with figures.
The image along with its pedestal [should be made] of eight parts of the door’s measure; / two parts of it are the image, and a third part is the pedestal.
The door is to be made by one who knows as less [than the waist] by an eighth part of the waist; / a third part should be the base, and a third part should be the waist;
and the spire is a third part of the temple, O mighty-armed one. / The sanctuary is expanded by a fourth part, and the door is likewise praised.
The wall should be made by one who knows as less than the sanctuary by an eighth part; / and it is praised as equal to a fourth part of the temple’s height.

3.18.m:
The plinth terrace, O king, [should be made] with two parts of the waist; / it should not be made excessively narrow, nor indeed too wide.
Just as it is according to the base, so should it be free from expansion above; / one should make a staircase adorned with lions on both sides, O king.
One should not make it flat-topped, nor pointed like a trident, nor bent; / it should be made even, delightful, and endowed with auspicious forms,
with a pinnacle beautifully whitened with plaster, decorated with varied waist ornaments, / with doorkeepers at the two door-posts, an even sanctum, uniform, / resembling a bhadrapīṭha, pleasing, smooth, and free from injury.
An image installed in a temple of such a kind will always bring good fortune; / it is constantly present in that manner, O hero among men; therefore this should be planned with diligent effort.

placing the astrologer at the front, the master builder should enter the forest; / then there he should examine, cut, and fell the lordly trees.
He should avoid a tree with hollows, entangled with creepers, eaten by worms, / and likewise one touched by fire or felled by wind,
and broken by an elephant, or those which are the dwellings of birds, / or near ascetics and watered with pot-water,

एते' प्रशस्ता विज्ञेया ये च सारा महीरुहाः ॥
शस्ताशस्ता न ये प्रोक्तास्ते तु मध्यफलाः स्मृताः॥11॥
रक्तसारा नरेन्द्राणां शुक्लसारा द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
पीतसारा विशां शस्ताः शूद्राणां कृष्णमध्यकाः॥12 ॥
छेत्तव्यं तु द्रुमं गत्वा सन्ध्याकाले तु पश्चिमे॥
द्रुमस्याग्रे बलिः कार्यो भूतानां तन्निवासिनाम्॥13॥
कुल्माषोल्लोपिकाभक्ष्यपुष्पधूपादिभिर्नृप ॥
कृत्वा चास्ये ततो मन्त्रमिदं यदुकुलोद्वह॥14॥
वसन्ति यत्र भूतानि तेभ्यः स्वस्ति नमोऽस्तु वः ॥
उपहारं गृहीत्वेमं क्रियतां वासपर्ययः ॥ 15 ॥
भवद्भिश्चाभ्यनुज्ञातः पूजितैः प्रमथेश्वराः ॥
देवागारे नियोक्ष्यामि द्रुममेतमसंशयम् ॥ 16 ॥
3.18.m:
arjuna, kadamba, madhūka, and also añjana, / devavṛkṣas, jātī trees, and indeed red sandalwood:
these are to be known as commended, as well as those trees having solid wood. / Those not declared as commended or uncommended are considered to yield middling results.
Trees with red heartwood are commended for kings; trees with white heartwood for the twice-born; / trees with yellow heartwood are beneficial for vaiśyas; and those with black cores for śūdras.
Having approached the tree to be cut at the time of evening twilight, / an offering must be made at the base of the tree to the spirits dwelling in it,
with gruel, cakes, edibles, flowers, incense, and the like, O king; / and then, O scion of the Yadu race, reciting this mantra at it:
‘Whichever spirits dwell here, hail to them, obeisance to you! / Having accepted this offering, let a change of abode be made.
Permitted by you, honored masters of Pramathas, / I shall surely employ this tree in the temple of the deity.

स्वप्नं वाप्यशुभं पश्येन्न तं भिन्द्यात्कथञ्चन ॥
छेत्तव्यं छेदयेद् वृक्षं कल्यमुत्थाय बुद्धिमान् ॥ 3.89.20 ॥
मध्वाज्याक्तेन राजेन्द्र ततः परशुना शुचिः ॥
रेखां प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पातयेत्प्रयतस्ततः ॥ 21 ॥
पूर्वाग्रमुत्तराग्रं वा पतनं तस्य शस्यते ॥
ऐशान्यां च महाराज दिक्षु शेषासु गर्हितम् ॥ 20 ॥
वामे प्रभग्ने न ग्राह्यं प्राणिहिंसाकरं तथा ॥
प्रशस्तं पतितं वृक्षं ग्राह्यं भवति यत्नतः ॥ 23 ॥
3.18.m:
If you do not abandon this tree, then through your favor / you should tell me the truth in a dream.’
Having spoken thus, the master builder should sleep right there, O king, / as well as the astrologer, O highly fortunate one, guarded by armed men.
Then, if during the night either of the two sees an auspicious dream, / O king, or sees nothing at all, he may cut the tree without a doubt.
If either sees an inauspicious dream, he must by no means cut it. / Rising at dawn, the wise man should fell the tree that is to be cut.
Then, pure, with an axe smeared with honey and ghee, O ruler of kings, / having made a line in pradakṣiṇa order, he should with restraint fell it.
Its falling with its tip toward the east or its tip toward the north is commended, / and in the north-east, O great king; in the remaining directions it is reprehensible.
If it breaks toward the left, it should not be taken, and likewise if it causes harm to living beings. / A fallen tree that is auspicious should be taken with care.

अग्रं मूलं प्रयत्नेन कर्तव्यं तस्य चिह्नितम् ॥
अग्रं देवस्य मूर्धानं पादं मूलं तु कारयेत् ॥ 24 ॥
अर्चाकृता विपर्यस्ता तिर्यग्वा मरणावहा ॥
अग्रमूलविपर्यासं स्तम्भानां च विवर्जयेत् ॥ 25 ॥
अग्रमूलविपर्यासे कृते वेश्म क्षयं व्रजेत् ॥
पूर्वाग्रा चोत्तराग्रा वा द्रुमा योज्या गृहेषु च ॥ 26 ॥
महावंशेषु वंशेषु विपर्यस्ता विगर्हिताः ॥
दक्षिणाग्राः पराग्रा वा गृहस्वामिविपत्तिदाः ॥ 27 ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन चिह्नैस्तं कारयेद्द्रुमम् ॥
अग्रे मूले च धर्मज्ञ ततः सम्यक्प्रवेशयेत् ॥ 28 ॥
शकटेन महाराज नरैर्वाप्यथ गोवृषैः ॥
आप्ते दिवसनक्षत्रे मुहूर्ते चाभिपूजिते ॥ 29 ॥
प्रविश्य सम्यक्तं विद्वान्यथायोगं नियोजयेत् ॥
यथोद्देशं महाराज स्थपतिर्लक्षणान्वितम् ॥ 3.89.30 ॥
3.18.m:
Its top and base must carefully be marked; / one should make the top into the head of the deity, and the base into the feet.
An image made upside down or sideways brings death. / And in pillars one should avoid an inversion of the top and base;
if an inversion of the top and base is made, the house will go to ruin. / Moreover, timbers used in houses should have their tips to the east or north;
in major beams and rafters, inverted ones are censured; / those with their tips to the south or the west bring calamity to the master of the house.
Therefore, with every effort, he should have that tree marked / at the top and base, O knower of dharma, and then bring it in properly,
on a cart, O great king, or by men, or by bulls, / at a favorable lunar mansion and day, and an honored muhūrta.
Having brought it in properly, the wise master builder should employ it / as appropriate according to its assignment, O great king, endowed with characteristics.

मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥

शैलं गत्वा महाराज दैवज्ञः स्थपतिस्तथा ॥ 1 ॥
शुक्ला शस्ता द्विजातीनां क्षत्त्रियाणां च लोहिता ॥
विशां पीता हिता कृष्णा शूद्राणां च हितप्रदा ॥ 2 ॥
एकवर्णां समां स्निग्धां निमग्नां च तथा क्षितौ ॥
घातातिमात्र स्फुटनां दृढां मृद्वीं मनोरमाम् ॥3 ॥

द्रुमच्छायोपगूढां च तीर्थाश्रयसमन्विताम ॥

3.18.m:
For having thus performed the entry into the forest, whoever brings timber and builds houses, / his foremost prosperity, O king, will always increase with wealth, grain, and sons.
3.90
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having gone by the rule previously stated, he should then examine stone. / Having gone to a mountain, O great king, the astrologer and the master builder:
White stone is commended for the twice-born, and red for kṣatriyas; / yellow is beneficial for vaiśyas, and black brings welfare to śūdras.
Of a single color, even, glossy, sunk deep in the ground, / splitting only under extreme blow, firm, smooth, pleasing,
soft, free of gravel, agreeable to the eye and mind, / washed by river water, pure, having dwelt in water,
embraced by the shade of trees, and associated with a sacred ford, / abundant in length and circumference—the wise say that such [stone] should be taken.
Unfit to be taken is that licked by fire, heated by the rays of the sun, / already used for another work, or touched by alkaline water,

अत्यन्तोपहतां रूक्षामपुण्यजनसेविताम ॥
तिलैः सम्भूषिता या तु विचित्रबिन्दुभिश्चिता ॥7॥
रेखामण्डलसङ्कीर्णां विद्धां विमलसंयुताम ॥
विमलं त्रिविधं ज्ञेयं लोहं कांस्यं च हेमजम् ॥ 8 ॥
या लोहविमलैर्जुष्टा सा जनक्षयकारिणी ॥
कांस्याभविमलोपेता जनमानविनाशिनी ॥ 9 ॥
हैमेन युक्ता दुर्भिक्षं तथा कुर्यादवग्रहम् ॥
धर्षणे च्छेदने चैव मण्डलं यत्प्रदृश्यते ॥ 3.90.10 ॥

मांजिष्ठवर्णसंकाशे गर्भे भवति दर्दुरः ॥ 11 ॥

एवं गर्भास्तु विज्ञेया बाह्यलक्षणलक्षिताः ॥ 14 ॥

बाह्यतो लक्षणं नास्ति तेषां लेपानि दापयेत ॥
ब्राह्मीं माहेश्वरीं शाक्रीं वैष्णवीं तक्षणोचिताम् ॥ 15 ॥
अजास्तन्येन संयोज्य शिलालेपं तु दापयेत् ॥
अहोरात्रे गते यत्र शिलालेपो न जायते ॥ 16 ॥
सगर्भां तां विजानीयात्प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत ॥
कासीसं पीतकासीसं गव्यक्षीरेण पेषयेत् ॥ 17 ॥
पाषाणं लेपितं तेन बहुवर्णं यदा भवेत ॥
सा शिला न प्रशस्ता स्यात्प्राणिगर्भा तु सा स्मृता ॥ 18 ॥
मुस्तकं करवीरं च कुष्ठं तालीशपत्रकम ॥
स्त्रीस्तन्यपिष्टैरेतैस्तु पाषाणं लेपयेद्बुधः ॥ 19 ॥
एभिर्लेपितमश्मानं यदा सिमिसिमायते ॥
कालकूटं विषं तत्र न तं हस्तेन संस्पृशेत् ॥ 3.90.20 ॥
श्वेतश्च पद्मवर्णश्च कुसुमोषणसन्निभः ॥
पाण्डुरो मुद्गवर्णश्च कापोतो भृङ्गसन्निभः ॥ 21 ॥
3.18.m:
If there is no external sign on them, he should apply pastes: / to the brāhmī, the māheśvarī, the śākrī, and the vaiṣṇavī [stones] that are suitable for carving. 15
Having mixed it with goat's milk, one should apply the paste to the stone. / When a day and night have passed, where the coating does not stick to the stone, 16
one should know that it contains an interior flaw, and avoid it with care. / One should grind green vitriol and yellow vitriol with cow's milk. 17
When a stone smeared with that becomes multicolored, / that stone would not be auspicious; it is said to have an animal within it. 18
Mustaka grass, oleander, costus, and tālīśa leaves— / with these ground with woman's breast-milk the wise man should smear the stone. 19
When the stone smeared with these boils up and hisses, / kālakūṭa poison is there; he should not touch it with his hand. 20
White, lotus-colored, resembling flower of pepper, / pale yellow, mung-bean-colored, pigeon-colored, and resembling a bee: 21

ज्ञेयाः प्रशस्ताः पाषाणाः अष्टावेते न संशयः ॥
कृष्णवर्णा शिला या तु शुक्ला हीरकसंयुता ॥ 22 ॥
सा शिला श्रीकरी ज्ञेया पुत्रपौत्रविवर्धिनी ॥
सितवर्णा तु या कृष्णैर्हीरकैः सबलीकृता॥ 23 ॥
बहुदोषकरी सा तु कृष्णा वा रक्तहीरकैः ॥
सर्ववर्णेषु शुक्लेषु प्रशस्तं हीरकं विदुः॥ 24 ॥
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानामन्यवर्णं विगर्हितम् ॥
ब्राह्मीं शिलां दिने गत्वा शोभने धूपयेद्बुधः ॥ 25 ॥
क्षीरेण नृप गव्येन सकषायैस्तथा जलैः ॥
आच्छाद्य कुसुमैर्दर्भैः प्राग्वत्कुर्यात्तथा बलिम्॥26॥
स्वप्नार्थं च स्वपेत्तत्र दैवज्ञः स्थपतिस्तथा ॥
प्राग्वद्दृष्टे शुभे स्वप्ने शिला नेया तु सा भवेत् ॥ 27 ॥
अदृष्टे तु तथा स्वप्ने न दुष्टे शोभनं भवेत् ॥
पूजनं तु द्वितीयेऽह्नि कृत्वा भाण्डगणस्य तु ॥ 28 ॥
3.18.m:
these eight stones should be known as auspicious, without a doubt. / A stone that is black in color, white, or possessed of diamonds, 22
that stone is known to bring prosperity and to multiply sons and grandsons. / But one of white color that is variegated with black diamonds 23
causes many troubles, or a black one with red diamonds. / Among all colors, diamonds are considered auspicious in white stones. 24
For stones of every color, [diamonds] of a different color are condemned. / Going to a brāhmī stone on an auspicious day, the wise man should cense it, 25
with cow's milk, O king, and with astringent waters. / Covering it with flowers and darbha grass, he should offer an oblation as before. 26
And the astrologer and the master-builder should sleep there for the sake of a dream. / When an auspicious dream is seen as before, that stone may be taken. 27
If no dream is seen, or if a bad one is seen, it will not be auspicious. / Having performed the worship of the set of tools on the second day, 28

3.18.m:
and then [honoring] the stone-cutter, he should bring it in, conveying it / just as before, O king, as was described regarding trees. 29
The knowledge of interior flaws of stones that has been stated, O best of kings— / know that all of that applies with effort to trees as well. 30
A stone acquired by this proper procedure will bring all happiness; / therefore one should indeed carry out with care all this entry into the forest as stated. 31
